questions.stem: A DNA sample is 30% adenine. What percentage is guanine?
questions.explanation: Chargaff: A = T = 30%, so G + C = 40% and G = 20%. A: 30% is thymine. B: 40% is G + C combined. D: 35% splits the remaining 70% without subtracting thymine. E: Halves the correct value.

questions.stem: Five double-stranded DNA fragments of equal length differ only in base composition. Which needs the most heat to denature?
questions.explanation: By Chargaff's rule, 15% A means 30% A–T and 70% G–C, the highest; G–C pairs have 3 hydrogen bonds versus 2 for A–T. A: 80% A–T, so only 20% G–C. C: 60% A–T, so 40% G–C. D: 40% G–C. E: 50% G–C.

questions.stem: Which feature is true of the mitochondrial genome but not of the nuclear genome?

options.B: More than 90% of the sequence is noncoding
options.C: Lower mutation rate than the other genome
options.D: Some codons don't follow the universal code

questions.explanation: Per the comparison slide, some mitochondrial codons deviate from the universal code. A: mtDNA is circular; nuclear DNA is linear. B: Only ~3% of mtDNA is noncoding; >90% describes nuclear DNA. C: mtDNA has a higher mutation rate. E: Both genomes are double-stranded.

questions.stem: A drug inhibits histone deacetylases. What is the expected effect on chromatin near target genes?

options.A: Chromatin stays acetylated and open, increasing transcription
options.C: Histone tails keep a stronger positive charge

questions.explanation: Acetylation neutralizes histone tails, loosening chromatin; blocking deacetylation keeps genes active. B: That's the effect of deacetylation. C: Acetylation removes positive charge. D: HDAC inhibition doesn't directly methylate DNA. E: Nucleosomes remain.

questions.stem: At one level of compaction, DNA is about 50 times shorter than its extended form, with about 6 nucleosomes per turn. Which level is this?
questions.explanation: The 2nd level, the 30-nm solenoid, shortens DNA ~50-fold with 6 nucleosomes per turn. A: Nucleosomes (1st level) shorten DNA ~7-fold. B: Loops are the 3rd level, formed by supercoiling the solenoid. C: Euchromatin is the decondensed, transcriptionally active state. D: The octamer is the protein core DNA wraps around in a nucleosome.

questions.stem: Whose X-ray diffraction image (Photo 51) confirmed the helical structure that Watson and Crick had only theorized?
questions.explanation: Franklin's Photo 51 revealed the helical structure. B: Wilkins, her colleague, showed her work to Watson and Crick and shared the 1962 Nobel Prize. C: Stimson showed the bases lie inside the molecule. D: Chargaff described the base-pairing ratios. E: Levene proposed the incorrect tetranucleotide model.

questions.stem: A molecule consists of deoxyribose bonded to adenine, with no phosphate group. What is it?
questions.explanation: Sugar + base = nucleoside, and adenine is a purine. A: A nucleotide also needs a phosphate. C: Adenine is a purine, not a pyrimidine. D: Wrong base class, and there is no phosphate. E: A free base has no sugar.
